Data: [TidyTuesday 2026-11-10](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-11-10).

Cited Feats ranks characters inside 21 franchises, and each placement rests on citations to the works.
Every citation is graded as shown on page or screen, stated by a character or a narrator, or scaled by comparison with someone else's feat.
The table adds up those grades for each franchise, and beside them it lists the deaths that ranked characters caused.

The share of shown evidence goes from 13% in Dungeons & Dragons to 95% in Berserk, and it is 59% over all 1,746 citations.
The lowest shares belong to Dungeons & Dragons, Warhammer 40,000 and Pokémon, which are tabletop and video game worlds where much of the lore sits in rulebooks and guidebooks.
The highest belong to Berserk, Dragon Ball, Godzilla and Bleach, which are told in comics and animation, where a feat is drawn.
Only two citations are scaled, one in Jujutsu Kaisen and one in Digimon, so that grade hardly changes the picture.

The deaths tell a different story.
Of the 307 recorded deaths, 40 are undone later in the story, and most of them sit in three franchises: Marvel with 13 of 49, Solo Leveling with 9 of 39, and Overlord with 5 of 20.
Their shares of shown evidence are 70%, 49% and 73%, so a franchise that shows more of its feats does not take fewer deaths back.
Westeros records the most deaths, 67, and undoes only 2.

Some cautions.
The ranks and grades are the editorial judgements of one fan-run site, not measurements.
The count of citations goes from 21 in Godzilla to 314 in Westeros, and 13 franchises have 5 recorded deaths or fewer, so their rows can move with a single entry.
